testedDecision: Classify which Stage 1 discharge-list findings are medication discrepancies requiring prescriber clarification before the discharge prescriptions are transmitted.
reason: The exposed Stage 2 note states outright that the enoxaparin entry was unintended and that the metformin 1000 mg entry auto-populated and should read 500 mg twice daily, naming exactly the two rows keyed as needing clarification. The Stage 3 note repeats that enoxaparin was removed and the metformin dose corrected, leaving the three benign rows eliminated without any list comparison. Sorting the matrix becomes reading ahead rather than reconciling the home list, the MAR, and the discharge list.

testedDecision: Choose the nurse first action after finding the discharge-list discrepancies, namely holding transmission and clarifying both with the prescriber.
reason: Stage 2 narrates the keyed action itself, showing the nurse contacting the covering resident and the prescriptions remaining on hold while the metformin entry is checked. A learner who has read it matches that narrative to the hold-and-clarify option instead of weighing nursing scope against the three distractors. The corrected orders that follow also confirm that transmitting the list or editing it independently was wrong.

testedDecision: Select appropriate nursing actions when the prescriber is uncertain about the metformin dose and disowns the enoxaparin discharge entry.
reason: The part stem carries only the resident uncertainty, while the rest of the exposed Stage 2 note performs each keyed action in turn, requesting pharmacist reconciliation, keeping prescriptions on hold, and having the resident enter corrected orders. That narrative also kills the distractor in which the nurse deletes enoxaparin herself, since the removal is shown happening by prescriber order. Stage 3 teaching discredits the continue-both-anticoagulants distractor by describing the family being told the injections stop at home.

testedDecision: Sequence verifying the corrected discharge list, confirming the safety-critical corrections, teaching, teach-back, and documentation after corrected orders are entered.
reason: The stem places the learner after the corrections, so Stage 2 legitimately supplies the corrected entries and INR follow-up that the confirmation step asks the nurse to verify. Stage 3 then narrates the tail of the keyed order in sequence, verified list first, then review of each medication with the client and daughter, then teach-back and confirmed appointments. That turns the ordering judgment into recall of an already-written sequence.
